cves.description:
Rapid7 Metasploit Framework versions prior to 6.5.10 suffer from an Improper Access Control issue in the msfdb database initialisation component whereby a PostgreSQL cluster initialised via msfdb init is configured with trust authentication and a world-accessible Unix domain socket in /tmp, allowing any local user on the same host to authenticate as the passwordless postgres superuser and execute arbitrary operating system commands as the msfdb owner. 


This issue is fixed in version 6.5.10.

PMB 7.3.1 before 7.3.15 and 7.4.x before 7.4.5 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject script through unescaped POST parameter names. Attackers can send crafted parameter names to opac_css/index.php extended_search, which empr.inc.php and languages.inc.php reflect into hidden form inputs to execute JavaScript. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-23.

Reddit Top RSS through commit 5e38bfd contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject scripts through the unescaped score GET parameter. Attackers can craft links with a score value that closes the input value attribute in html.php, executing JavaScript in victims' browsers. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-19.

JoomBri Careers 3.3.0 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject scripts through the 'keyword' parameter of the /for-jobseekers/search-jobs endpoint in com_jbcareers. Attackers can craft malicious URLs using an attribute-breakout payload with onfocus and autofocus to execute arbitrary JavaScript and steal session tokens or credentials. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-23.

Tiki Wiki CMS Groupware 12.12 through 12.14, 15.5 before 18.10, 19.0 before 21.9, 22.0 before 24.3, and 25.0 contain a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject scripts through the objectId parameter of tiki-ajax_services.php. Attackers can send a crafted GET request with the comment controller and list action to execute arbitrary JavaScript and steal session tokens or credentials. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-19.

phpLDAPadmin 1.1.0 before 1.2.5 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject scripts through the dn parameter of cmd.php?cmd=template_engine. Attackers can supply an unparseable dn value that pretty_print_dn returns unescaped in the 'No such entry' error, executing JavaScript in victims' browsers. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-23.

Bagisto 2.1.0 before 2.2.1 contains a client-side template injection vulnerability in the search page where the 'query' parameter is rendered unescaped inside a Vue app root. Unauthenticated attackers can send crafted VueJS template expressions to the /bagisto-common/search endpoint via the 'query' parameter to execute arbitrary JavaScript in victims' browsers. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2024-07-30.

When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured as a mail proxy, undisclosed traffic can cause a use-after-free in an nginx worker process. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR.

Impact:
A remote unauthenticated attacker may crash an nginx worker process or corrupt its memory, disrupting service. Remote code execution is a potential impact. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

When using the listen directive with the ssl parameter in the http block with TLSv1.3 enabled, an attacker can use a specially crafted TLS connection to cause an infinite loop in the NGINX worker process while reading the HTTP request body. As a result, the worker process stops accepting new connections and processing existing connections. Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

Impact: This vulnerability allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) of NGINX. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured to require client certificates ("ssl_verify_client on") in a non-default stream virtual server, a remote attacker could bypass verification of client certificates.

Impact:
An attacker could leverage this vulnerability to bypass verification of client certificates. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured to use the ngx_stream_ssl_module module with dynamic certificate loading and the ngx_stream_proxy_module module with the proxy_protocol v2 directive, an abbreviated SSL handshake can cause a worker process to terminate.

Impact:
This vulnerability may allow remote attackers to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the NGINX system. This is a data plane vulnerability only; there is no control plane exposure.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

Description:
This issue affects NGINX Plus and NGINX Open Source configurations that use HTTP/3. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can cause a use-after-free condition in the NGINX worker process, leading to a restart. Exploitation also depends on conditions beyond the attacker’s control. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR.

Impact:
This vulnerability may allow remote attackers to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the NGINX system or to possibly trigger a code execution. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

This issue affects NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source configurations that use HTTP/2. When NGINX processes undisclosed traffic, the flow control window can exceed the allowed threshold, potentially resulting in a heap buffer overflow typically followed by an NGINX worker segmentation fault. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR.

Impact: An attacker could leverage this vulnerability to crash the NGINX worker process, corrupt its memory, or potentially execute code remotely. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured to use HTTP/2 for client connections and proxy client requests to a backend, a specially crafted request can result in use-after-free in the worker process, if this process is running low on worker_connections. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR.




Impact:



This vulnerability may allow remote attackers to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the NGINX system or may allow a code execution. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

This issue occurs when NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured as a proxy, the proxied server name includes variables, and a Server Side Includes (SSI) or mirror directive sends a subrequest to a location that resolves the same server name. Under these conditions, a specially crafted HTTP request may cause a use-after-free condition in a worker process. An attacker may also be able to execute code if Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) is disabled or the attacker can bypass ASLR.

Impact: 
An attacker could leverage this vulnerability to crash the NGINX worker process, corrupt its memory, or perform remote code execution (RCE)



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

Description
When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured with the ngx_stream_ssl_preread_module module, a specially crafted ClientHello message from an unauthenticated attacker causes forged values of the ngx_stream_ssl_preread_module variables, affecting virtual server selection. In addition, it may also cause a disagreement with a proxied server terminating the SSL/TLS connection without Transport Layer Security (TLS) 1.3 support.

Impact
This vulnerability may allow an attacker to forge values of the ngx_stream_ssl_preread_module variables and bypass the NGINX systems stream routing segmentation. As a result, the attacker may be able to route the connection to a privileged or internal backend that should be unreachable and gain access to sensitive information. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.






Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured to use the try_files and alias directives with a map variable, certain combinations of regular expression captures in map and try_files can cause a segmentation fault in an NGINX worker process.

Impact:
An attacker could leverage this vulnerability to cause an NGINX worker process to terminate unexpectedly. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

Retool versions 3.253.0 before 3.253.19, 3.254.0 before 3.284.12, and 3.285.0 before 3.300.4 contain a DOM-based cross-site scripting vulnerability in the custom-component-collections.html postMessage handler that imports received code without origin validation. Unauthenticated attackers can send crafted postMessage events that load attacker-controlled code via data:text/javascript URIs to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's context. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2026-04-22.

cPanel & WHM 11.134.0.13 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject scripts through the mpidentity parameter of /mailman/listinfo. Attackers can send crafted requests with a script-context breakout payload in mpidentity to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's browser. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2026-06-08.

Optimizely Web Experimentation before 2026-11-17 mishandles the account signup flow, leading to presence of attacker-controlled code in the projectJS (aka Project JavaScript) field of certain cdn.optimizely.com assets.

A Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability in OpenKM v6.3.12 allows attackers to execute arbitrary Javascript in the context of the user's browser via a crafted input injected into the Content parameter.

k8s-mcp-server manages Kubernetes clusters through the Model Context Protocol. Prior to 1.1.0, SERVER_MODE defaults to SSE, with the listener on 0.0.0.0:8080, but main.go creates the SSE server without an authentication option or context function. The GET /sse handler creates a sessionId that is only a correlation value, and the POST /message handler accepts a loadable sessionId without an authorization or Origin check before dispatching tools/call; consequently, any client able to reach the port can enumerate and invoke registered Kubernetes tools without credentials. Read-only mode is disabled by default, leaving write-capable Kubernetes tools available to run with the server's configured cluster privileges. This issue is fixed in version 1.1.0.

Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability in winCRM. Exploiting this vulnerability could allow a remote user to send a specially crafted URL to the victim and steal their session data by allowing JavaScript code to be injected in 'Tarea' parameter in '/Tareas/TareasCrear?ddv=cal'.
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.1.3, 2025.11.7 missing authorization in the Kubernetes integration allowed project viewers to use stored credentials
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.1.3, 2025.11.7 stored XSS on the Docker Container Info tab was possible

A stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the Public News Article Rendering Module of PHPGurukul News Portal Project v4.1 allows authenticated attackers with administrative or sub-administrative privileges to inject arbitrary HTML and JavaScript through the postdescription parameter when creating or editing news articles. The application renders the stored post content without proper output encoding in news-details.php, allowing injected JavaScript to execute in the browsers of users who visit the affected article.

A Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability exists in PHPGurukul News Portal Project V4.1. The $currenturl variable in news-details.php is constructed using unencoded REQUEST_URI and HTTP_HOST server variables and echoed directly into the href attributes of social share links. An unauthenticated remote attacker can exploit this by crafting a URL containing HTML metacharacters to break out of the href attribute and execute arbitrary HTML or JavaScript in the context of the victim's browser.

pnpm exe before 10.34.8 embeds an outdated Node.js runtime that still trusts compromised eMudhra intermediate CA certificates during registry TLS connections. Network attackers holding a recovered intermediate key can intercept standalone pnpm registry fetches and serve forged package metadata or tarballs.

Obot from 0.9.0 before 0.27.0 contains a command injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users to execute shell commands by embedding an EOF line in file-type MCP server configuration values. Attackers can terminate the heredoc in the generated init container script to run commands, modify the MCP server files volume, and reach services on Obot's Docker network.

SemanticMediaWiki from 3.0.0 before 7.4.0 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in CsvFileExportPrinter and DsvResultPrinter via unescaped valuesep and separator parameters. Attackers can craft Special:Ask links using request_type=special_page so export output renders as text/html, executing JavaScript in victims' browsers under the wiki origin.

SemanticMediaWiki from 2.5.0 before 7.4.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows users with the smw-patternedit right to inject script by seeding markup reference names in MediaWiki:Smw_allows_pattern. Once an editor annotates the matching Allows pattern value, AllowsPatternValue emits it unescaped on Special:Browse, executing JavaScript in every viewer's session.

The Datadog Agent collects events and metrics from hosts and sends them to Datadog. Prior to datadog-apm-inject 0.66.0, the Datadog Single Step Instrumentation injector stores helper tooling in a predictable host directory. On Linux or Kubernetes systems with SSI enabled and at least one Java service instrumented through SSI, a local unprivileged attacker with shell access to the same host can influence that tooling and execute code with the privileges of the instrumented Java service. Services that use dd-java-agent without SSI and non-Java language runtimes are not affected. This issue is fixed in datadog-apm-inject 0.66.0.

cf-manager is an all-in-one dashboard for managing multiple Cloudflare accounts and services. Prior to 1.1.2, worker/src/routes/workers.ts uses bare fetch(url) calls to retrieve user-supplied URLs and deploys the returned content as a Worker script using stored Cloudflare credentials. The multipart and JSON branches of POST /api/:accountId/workers and POST /api/batch-deploy accept URLs without protocol, destination, redirect, content-type, or response-size validation. An attacker with deployment API access, or unauthenticated access when API_SECRET is not configured, can make cf-manager access internal resources or fetch attacker-controlled JavaScript and execute it in the victim Cloudflare Workers account. This issue is fixed in version 1.1.2.

LLMKube is a Kubernetes operator for self-hosted large language model inference across heterogeneous hardware. Prior to 0.9.0, the ModelReconciler accepts arbitrary absolute paths and file:// URIs in Model.spec.source without restricting them to approved roots. A namespace user who can create or update Model and InferenceService resources can cause copyLocalModel to open an attacker-selected file in the controller pod or cause a HostPathVolumeSource to mount an attacker-selected node file when modelCache.enabled is enabled, which is the default. The selected file is copied into model storage and can expose controller service-account credentials or other node secrets outside the attacker's namespace. This issue is fixed in version 0.9.0.

cassandra-jdbc-wrapper provides a JDBC-compliant API over the Java driver for Apache Cassandra. Prior to 4.16.4 and 5.0.2, DriverUtil.toStringWithoutSensitiveValues() and DriverUtil.redactSensitiveValuesInJdbcUrl() redact the password property but not the equally sensitive token property used for DataStax Astra and other token-based authentication. When DEBUG logging is enabled, SessionHolder passes connection properties and JDBC URLs containing token through these helpers, causing the live token to be written in plaintext when connections are acquired or released. An attacker who can read those logs can use the token to access Cassandra data and operations authorized to that credential. This issue is fixed in versions 4.16.4 and 5.0.2.

IBM Engineering AI Hub 1.0.0 through 1.4.0 is vulnerable to cross-site scripting. This vulnerability allows an unauthenticated attacker to embed arbitrary JavaScript code in the Web UI thus altering the intended functionality potentially leading to credentials disclosure within a trusted session.

MyMangaDB is a self-hosted manga collection manager with automatic metadata, MyAnimeList import, Docker support, and collection statistics. Prior to 2.7.2, the unauthenticated /api/v1/database/export handler in backend/app/api/v1/endpoints/database.py returns a ZIP containing the live SQLite database and the cover-image library. The database includes the users table and hashed_password values, allowing a remote attacker to obtain all application data and conduct offline password attacks without a session or token. This issue is fixed in version 2.7.2.

MyMangaDB is a self-hosted manga collection manager with automatic metadata, MyAnimeList import, Docker support, and collection statistics. Prior to 2.7.2, the unauthenticated /api/v1/images/manga/save handler in backend/app/api/v1/endpoints/image.py accepts a client-controlled filename and joins it to IMAGE_SAVE_PATH without confining the result. Traversal sequences can escape the image directory and overwrite process-writable files, including DATABASE_PATH for the live SQLite database, while the client-supplied image content type does not validate the uploaded bytes. An attacker can replace the database to plant an administrative user and can overwrite other writable files, causing full application compromise and availability loss. This issue is fixed in version 2.7.2.

MyMangaDB is a self-hosted manga collection manager with automatic metadata, MyAnimeList import, Docker support, and collection statistics. Prior to 2.7.2, the unauthenticated /api/v1/database/import handler in backend/app/api/v1/endpoints/database.py accepts a ZIP archive and moves an included database file to DATABASE_PATH while also replacing IMAGE_PATH content. An attacker can supply a database containing an attacker-controlled users table and administrative account, then authenticate as that account; invalid replacement data can also destroy application data or availability. This issue is fixed in version 2.7.2.

Dokploy is a free, self-hostable Platform as a Service (PaaS). Prior to 0.31.1, the database password validation used by the MySQL, PostgreSQL, MariaDB, MongoDB, and Redis change-password procedures permits backticks, and the procedures interpolate attacker-controlled passwords into Bash command strings. An authenticated user who can update a database password can trigger command substitution before the database command runs, resulting in arbitrary operating-system command execution with the Dokploy process privileges, which are typically root. This issue is fixed in version 0.31.1.

keystore-go is a Go implementation of the Java KeyStore encoder and decoder. In 2.1.0 and earlier, keystore.Decode in decoder.go does not check the error returned when reading the trailing SHA-1 integrity digest and bounds its comparison by the length of the digest actually read. If an attacker with write access removes the final 20-byte digest from a modified JKS file, the empty actual digest causes the comparison loop to execute zero times and Decode returns the parsed keystore without an error. For certificate-only stores using TrustedCertificateEntry values, this bypasses both tamper detection and password verification, allowing trusted CA certificates to be added or replaced without knowing the keystore password and potentially enabling interception or modification of TLS connections that trust the forged CA. This issue is fixed in version 3.0.0.

Dokploy is a free, self-hostable Platform as a Service (PaaS). From 0.29.13 until 0.31.0, the Docker terminal, container-log, and monitoring WebSocket handlers accept a caller-controlled serviceId as authorization but do not consistently bind the requested containerId or appName to that service. A member with read access to any service can consequently target unrelated containers, obtain a root shell in the Dokploy panel container, read other tenants' logs and statistics, and use the mounted Docker socket to compromise the host. This issue is fixed in version 0.31.0.

Dokploy is a free, self-hostable Platform as a Service (PaaS). Prior to 0.31.1, the Nixpacks publishDirectory build setting accepts shell metacharacters and is interpolated into a docker cp command executed through child_process.exec. An authenticated user with access to an application can execute arbitrary commands on the Dokploy host when triggering a Nixpacks deployment, leading to host compromise through the privileged Docker environment. This issue is fixed in version 0.31.1.

Dokploy is a free, self-hostable Platform as a Service (PaaS). Prior to 0.31.1, every network.* procedure is only authentication-protected and does not require the Docker permission, allowing a standard member to list, inspect, create, import, recreate, resynchronize, and delete Docker networks. A member can disrupt service connectivity or alter network configuration, and create/import operations can target an unchecked serverId. This issue is fixed in version 0.31.1.

Dokploy is a free, self-hostable Platform as a Service (PaaS). Prior to 0.31.1, the backup prefix field is only checked for a nonempty value, and normalizeS3Path preserves shell metacharacters before the prefix is interpolated into rclone upload and retention-cleanup command strings. An authenticated organization member with backup permission for a service can execute arbitrary commands as root on the Dokploy host or configured remote server when a PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, MongoDB, libSQL, Compose, or web-server backup runs manually, on schedule, or performs retention cleanup. This issue is fixed in version 0.31.1.

ScreenTinker before 3.2.4 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the GET /api/kiosk/:id/render endpoint that allows users with kiosk page edit rights to store javascript: URLs in page buttons. Attackers can trigger script execution in the dashboard origin when an administrator activates the button, hijacking the victim's session and taking full control of the instance.

A security vulnerability has been detected in yangzongzhuan RuoYi up to 4.8.3. The impacted element is an unknown function of the file ruoyi-admin/src/main/java/com/ruoyi/web/controller/system/SysLoginController.java of the component User Registration Endpoint. The manipulation of the argument deptId/status/userId/createBy leads to improper input validation. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The exploit has been disclosed publicly and may be used. The identifier of the patch is d7ad977c9ca64e9b081c893ec56fe08f51f66698. It is recommended to apply a patch to fix this issue.

Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory in the Como log viewer in Temenos Application Framework Java (TAFJ) R18.SP76.0 allows remote authenticated attackers to read arbitrary files via path traversal

Cross-site scripting in the embedded co-browsing feature in Unblu inc. Unblu Spark 7.0 through 7.57.9 and 8.0 before 8.40.2, on on-premises and cloud deployments, allows an unauthenticated remote attacker in the visitor role to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the browser of an agent taking part in the attacker's co-browsing session, via manipulated synchronized page attributes of the co-browsed page.



The JavaScript runs in the context and under the identity of the agent's session in the Agent Desk or the Single Conversation Desk.



Exploitation requires an agent to join an embedded co-browsing session with the attacker. Mobile co-apping isn't affected.

In Eclipse Yasson versions 3.0 to 3.0.5, a race condition (CWE-362) exists in the handling of @JsonbNumberFormat. Yasson creates one java.text.NumberFormat instance per annotated property and shares it across all threads that use the same Jsonb instance. NumberFormat is not thread-safe, and the deserializer called parse() on it without synchronization. When multiple threads deserialize concurrently, a thread can receive a numeric value that belongs to another thread's input, receive an incorrect value, or fail with an exception. A remote attacker who can send concurrent requests to an application that deserializes untrusted JSON this way may cause incorrect data to be processed or cause another user's value to be returned. Exploitation requires that the application use @JsonbNumberFormat with a shared Jsonb instance and that the attacker win a timing race. This issue is fixed in version 3.0.6 by synchronizing access to the shared NumberFormat instances.
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2, 2026.1.4 remote code execution was possible via Kubernetes Executor settings
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2, 2026.1.4, 2025.11.8 stored XSS in the NPM Registry build feature was possible
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2, 2026.1.4, 2025.11.8 stored XSS in the npm connection health report was possible
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2 reflected XSS in Kubernetes cloud profile namespace and deployment choosers was possible

In Eclipse Ditto versions 1.1.0 to 3.9.8, when pre-authentication is enabled, the gateway service accepts the pre-authenticated subject not only from the `x-ditto-pre-authenticated` HTTP header set by a trusted reverse proxy, but also from an undocumented `x-ditto-pre-authenticated` URL query parameter that a client can set. A reverse proxy that only overwrites the header therefore does not stop clients from supplying their own subject. With the default configuration of the Ditto Helm chart (`global.jwtOnly: false`, which implicitly enables pre-authentication), the bundled nginx skips HTTP Basic authentication for any request with an `Authorization: Bearer` header and forwards it without the pre-authentication header. An unauthenticated remote attacker can send an invalid Bearer token together with the query parameter to authenticate as any chosen policy subject. Pre-authentication succeeds before the JWT is validated, so the attacker can read and modify Things and Policies with that subject's permissions. As a mitigation, disable pre-authentication in the gateway (`ENABLE_PRE_AUTHENTICATION=false`) or, when using the Helm chart, configure `global.jwtOnly: true`.

PHP-FPM request smuggling through an unread HTTP request body.

PHP does not discard the unread part of an HTTP request body at request shutdown when the application has opened php://input without reading it to the end. When the front end reuses backend connections, which is not the default in nginx or Apache (for example nginx with fastcgi_keep_conn on, or Apache mod_proxy_fcgi with enablereuse=on), PHP-FPM can parse the leftover bytes as a new FastCGI request. An unauthenticated remote attacker can use a single crafted multipart/form-data request to forge a backend request with chosen parameters such as SCRIPT_FILENAME, REMOTE_ADDR and PHP_ADMIN_VALUE, which can lead to execution of attacker-controlled PHP code. With LSAPI, subsequent requests on the connection can be disrupted.

This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

PHP-FPM epoll use-after-free can lead to local privilege escalation.

When catch_workers_output is enabled and the epoll event backend is used, the PHP-FPM master can close a worker's output pipe in fpm_child_close() without removing the associated event, and the delayed cleanup can free the worker record while its epoll registration is still active. A later event is then dispatched through a pointer into freed memory. A local attacker who can execute PHP code in an FPM worker can crash the master or execute code with its privileges, commonly root. catch_workers_output is disabled by default but enabled in the official PHP-FPM Docker images.

This issue affects PHP versions from 8.1.20 through 8.1.34, from 8.2.7 before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

PHP-FPM status endpoint XSS via unescaped user and script fields.

The PHP-FPM full status output includes the request method, authentication user and script filename of each worker without escaping them for the HTML, XML or JSON format. When the status endpoint is enabled, an unauthenticated remote attacker can store markup in a worker's scoreboard entry with an ordinary request, for example through the username of an HTTP Basic authentication header that the web server forwards to PHP-FPM, or through the script filename where the attacker can influence it. When a user views the full status page as HTML, the injected JavaScript runs in the origin of that page. The attacker does not need access to the status endpoint. Malformed XML or JSON output can also disrupt monitoring tools.

This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

modified eCommerce Shopsoftware through 3.3.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated administrators to inject scripts via the unsanitized products_model field. Attackers with product editing permission can store JavaScript that executes in browsers of other administrators, storefront visitors, and customers viewing carts and order history.

Tiptap @tiptap/core 2.0.0-alpha.0 before 3.30.4 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows attackers to inject DOM attributes via a __proto__ key passed to mergeAttributes(). Attackers can supply untrusted JSON attribute data whose __proto__ replaces the merged object's prototype, causing DOMSerializer.renderSpec to render injected event handlers that execute JavaScript.

WatchAlert 2.0.0 through 3.9.20 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in the /api/w8t/datasource/dataSourceGet endpoint that lets authenticated users read other tenants' datasources because lookups omit tenant_id filtering. Tenant members with datasource view permission can request another tenant's datasource ID to obtain basic auth passwords, AWS and Alibaba Cloud keys, and Kubernetes kubeconfigs.

parse5 7.0.0 before 8.1.1 contains an uncaught exception vulnerability in Preprocessor#_processSurrogate that allows remote attackers to crash applications by supplying two consecutive low surrogates. Attackers can submit input such as U+DC00 U+DC00, which decodes to out-of-range code point 0x110000 and throws a RangeError from parse, parseFragment, or streaming parsers, crashing Node.js processes.

@scalar/typebox before 0.1.4 contains a code injection vulnerability in TypeCompiler that allows attackers to execute JavaScript by supplying crafted schema strings. Attackers can inject single-quote breakouts into string format, Kind names, property keys or Literal values to run arbitrary JavaScript in the host Node.js process during Compile() and Check().

InfoScan fails to properly handle certain malformed or incomplete requests to its login and password-reset endpoints. These requests can trigger unhandled server exceptions that return detailed Node.js stack traces to the requester. The responses disclose internal filesystem paths, application directory names, source file locations, and line numbers.

NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. From 3.10.3 until 3.10.4, the NLTK 3.10.3 JVM hardening validates Java launcher tokens in the options channel but appends the caller-controlled cmd sequence without requiring its first token to be a main class. Supplying -jar or an @argfile through nltk.internals.java or StanfordSegmenter.java_class can therefore execute attacker-selected Java bytecode without the unsafe-JAR opt-in. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

A flaw was found in Keycloak. An authenticated remote user with a pending required security action, such as configuring multi-factor authentication (MFA), can bypass the mandatory action by submitting a specially crafted request to the consent endpoint without a valid session code. Keycloak incorrectly interprets the submission as a page refresh and completes the authentication process, allowing the user to access the application without fulfilling the required security policies.

pREST (PostgreSQL REST) is an API that delivers an application on top of a Postgres database. Prior to 2.4.0, the vulnerable parameter is _groupby, handled by GroupByClause in adapters/postgres/postgres.go. adapters/postgres/postgres.go uses the weaker isSafeSQLExpression check for this function-expression branch instead of the stricter single-field validator used for _select. That check validates only the outer function name against a 13-function allowlist and permits nested subqueries, trailing UNION syntax, and inner pg_ functions. controllers/crud.go concatenates the GROUP BY expression while parameterizing only WHERE values, allowing attacker-controlled SQL structure into the clause. Default configuration permits unauthenticated access; a restricted installation may require a low-privilege table reader. UNION-based extraction requires compatible column counts and types and was not verified end to end, but a delay-producing function can cause denial of service without that alignment. This issue is fixed in 2.4.0.

@fastify/http-proxy is a Fastify plugin that proxies HTTP and WebSocket traffic to an upstream server. In versions before 11.6.10, it rejects destinations containing parent-directory path segments by an exact string match, so a segment that carries a semicolon path parameter, such as a dot-dot segment followed by a semicolon and an optional parameter, is not equal to the plain dot-dot form and passes the check, and the WHATWG URL parser keeps it as an ordinary segment so the rewrite-prefix containment check also passes. Servlet containers such as Apache Tomcat and Jetty strip semicolon path parameters from each segment before resolving dot-segments, so a request routed through the configured prefix is rewritten and reaches the upstream where it resolves above the intended subtree, escaping the path the proxy is meant to expose and, on some containers, crossing application contexts. Both the HTTP and WebSocket proxy paths are affected. The issue is fixed in @fastify/http-proxy 11.6.10, and users should upgrade to 11.6.10 or later.

@fastify/reply-from is a Fastify plugin that forwards requests to an upstream HTTP server. In versions before 12.8.4, its buildURL function rejects parent-directory path segments by an exact string match, so a segment that carries a semicolon path parameter, such as a dot-dot segment followed by a semicolon and an optional parameter, is not equal to the plain dot-dot form and passes the traversal check, and the WHATWG URL parser keeps it as an ordinary segment so the base-prefix containment check also passes. Backends that strip semicolon path parameters before resolving dot-segments, such as Apache Tomcat, Jetty, WildFly, and Spring Boot, turn the segment back into a parent-directory reference and resolve it, so an unauthenticated client can escape the intended upstream prefix and reach internal paths such as admin or internal API endpoints, including with state-changing methods. Deployments that proxy to Node.js, nginx, or Express upstreams are not affected. The issue is fixed in @fastify/reply-from 12.8.4, and users should upgrade to 12.8.4 or later.

@fastify/http-proxy is a Fastify plugin that proxies HTTP and WebSocket traffic to an upstream server. In versions from 9.0.0 up to but not including 11.6.10, when the plugin is registered with websocket support enabled, it takes every upgraded socket and dispatches the request through the Fastify router before the WebSocket library takes ownership of the socket. Node.js removes its own error listener from the socket before emitting the upgrade event, and the plugin does not attach one of its own during routing, so a socket error such as a client connection reset that arrives before the WebSocket library takes over is unhandled and terminates the Node.js process. The error window is open whenever anything asynchronous runs between dispatch and the route handler, such as an async hook on the proxied route or any unrelated async route in the application. A single unauthenticated upgrade request followed by a connection reset is enough to crash the server, and it can be repeated to keep the process down. The issue is fixed in @fastify/http-proxy 11.6.10, and users should upgrade to 11.6.10 or later.

@fastify/http-proxy is a Fastify plugin that proxies HTTP and WebSocket traffic to an upstream server. In versions from 9.4.0 up to but not including 11.6.10, when the plugin is registered with websocket support enabled, a WebSocket upgrade request whose path carries a URL fragment is matched by the router and answered with a successful upgrade before the upstream link is created. Building the upstream target then throws, the error is only logged, and the accepted client socket is left open with no error listener, so the next frame the client sends becomes an unhandled error and terminates the Node.js process. A request target that is not a valid URL reference reaching a parameterized prefix triggers the same path. A single unauthenticated upgrade request followed by one frame is enough to crash the server, and it can be repeated to keep the process down. The issue is fixed in @fastify/http-proxy 11.6.10, and users should upgrade to 11.6.10 or later.

RepoManager is a self-hosted deb/rpm package repository. Prior to 5.13.3, a registered host or a party with its host/API credential can submit package metadata. Inventory reporting accepts package name and version, while available-update reporting accepts package name, version, and repository; the repository field exists only on that path. RepoManager stores these values, and stored values are rendered on the host's package detail page without preventing stored HTML or JavaScript from executing. An administrator must later view the page for script execution. The script runs in the administrator's authenticated browser session and can expose administrative data or forge privileged requests; the advisory describes possible escalation through admin-only functionality. Fixed in 5.13.3.

@fastify/http-proxy is a Fastify plugin that proxies HTTP and WebSocket traffic to an upstream server. In versions from 9.0.0 up to but not including 11.6.10, when the plugin is registered with websocket support enabled, a WebSocket upgrade that is pipelined behind another HTTP request on the same cleartext connection arrives while that request's response is still attached to the socket. The shared upgrade listener sees the socket is already claimed and returns early without taking the upgrade, but it does not attach an error listener to the raw socket, and Node.js has already removed its own error listener before emitting the upgrade event. A later socket error on that connection, such as a client connection reset, is therefore unhandled and terminates the Node.js process. A single unauthenticated connection that pipelines an upgrade behind a normal request and then resets is enough to crash the server, and it can be repeated to keep the process down. Upgrades over TLS are not affected. The issue is fixed in @fastify/http-proxy 11.6.10, and users should upgrade to 11.6.10 or later.

A reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability in WatchGuard Dimension's Device Configuration History page allows an authenticated attacker with view permission on a device to execute arbitrary JavaScript in another authenticated user's browser by enticing the victim to open a specially crafted link.

OpenRemote is an open-source internet-of-things platform. Prior to 1.31.0, an authenticated user who obtains another user's MQTT session ID can disconnect that session across realm boundaries through the GET route GET {realm}/disconnect/{sessionID}. In manager/src/main/java/org/openremote/manager/security/UserResourceImpl.java, disconnectUserSession ignores the requested realm and calls mqttBrokerService.disconnectSession(sessionID) without checking session ownership; model/src/main/java/org/openremote/model/security/UserResource.java exposes the route without an @RolesAllowed restriction. The earlier cross-realm read-method guards did not cover this disconnect method, and same-realm users can also disconnect sessions they do not own. Session IDs are not trivially brute-forceable but may be exposed through monitoring, logs, or correlated API calls, and the unauthorized disconnect can disrupt MQTT connectivity across tenant boundaries without directly disclosing session data. This issue is fixed in 1.31.0.

The MongoDB Node.js Driver does not neutralize NUL characters in the user name and password values it places into the message it builds for SASL PLAIN authentication. A party who can choose the login values that an application passes to the driver can alter where the fields of that message begin and end. This may result in a receiving system reading a login name and secret that differ from the values the application supplied. Authenticating as a different account still requires that account's password. Only deployments that use SASL PLAIN authentication are affected.

A weakness in the MongoDB Node.js driver can place sensitive information taken from an application-supplied connection string into the text of an error produced while that connection string is being parsed. The error is generated inside the application process before any database connection is made, so no database account and no network access are needed for it to occur. A party able to read the application's error output or log files may thereby obtain database credentials that the application's configuration source would otherwise keep to a narrower audience.

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.4, 10.2.8, 10.0.11, and 9.4.16, a low-privileged user who holds the "power" Splunk role could inject malicious content into a Splunk Web view. When another authenticated user opens the affected view in Splunk Web, the injected content executes unauthorized JavaScript code within the viewing user's browser session.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Web does not properly validate content in a view definition before rendering the view.
For more information see Define roles on the Splunk platform with capabilities (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.2/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/define-roles-on-the-splunk-platform-with-capabilities) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, an unauthenticated user with network-path interception capability could cause attacker-controlled JavaScript to run in the browser of a security analyst who previews a Portable Document Format (PDF) attachment in Mission Control. The JavaScript could expose data and perform actions available to the security analyst.
The vulnerability is possible because Mission Control loads the PDF rendering worker from an external content delivery network.
The vulnerability requires the unauthenticated user to intercept the network path to the external content delivery network and a security analyst to preview a PDF attachment in Mission Control. The unauthenticated user should not be able to exploit the vulnerability at will.
For more information see Collaborate on investigations in Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/administer/8.7/investigations/collaborate-on-investigations-in-splunk-enterprise-security) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user with edit permission for a container or workbook task could store attacker-controlled Hypertext Markup Language (HTML) in a note. When another user with view permission for the affected container and its notes opens the affected note in Mission Control, the note could run unauthorized JavaScript code in the browser of that user, expose data available through the authenticated session, and perform actions available through the authenticated session.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR does not neutralize active content in all notes before Mission Control renders them.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user with the containers:edit permission could import a container that includes a malicious Hypertext Markup Language (HTML) note. When another user views the imported note, Splunk SOAR could run unauthorized JavaScript in the browser of that user, exposing data and allowing actions available to that user.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR does not sanitize HTML note content during container import before it renders the content in Mission Control.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user with container edit permission could supply timestamps when creating containers and artifacts through the Representational State Transfer (REST) API. This could alter the timeline shown to analysts and cause configured data retention strategies to delete affected records earlier than intended.
The vulnerability is possible because the REST API accepts client-supplied values for timestamps that Splunk SOAR uses to order records and apply data retention.
The early deletion impact requires an applicable data retention strategy; the timeline impact does not.
For more information see Manage your PostgreSQL database with data retention strategies (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/6.4.0/manage-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-system-health-and-performance/manage-your-postgresql-database-with-data-retention-strategies) in the Splunk documentation.

Connaisseur is an admission controller that integrates container image signature verification into a Kubernetes cluster. Prior to 3.11.1, the Cosign validator counts valid signature layers rather than distinct trust roots for trustRoot: "*" policies using an explicit threshold or an implicit require-all policy. An attacker who controls one configured trust root's signing key and can attach multiple signatures to an image can satisfy a threshold intended to require multiple independent roots, causing admission without the intended signer quorum. Policies using a single trust root or the required option are not affected. This issue is fixed in 3.11.1.

A component of the MongoDB Java Driver that processes connection configuration places credential values taken from that configuration into generated text and error output without replacing them with a placeholder, unlike other parts of the driver. A party able to read output produced by an application that embeds the driver may obtain database or proxy credentials in clear text.

The MongoDB Java driver applies its DNS seedlist domain restriction to a record value that is later re-interpreted differently when the connection target is parsed, so the name that is checked and the name that is used can differ. An unauthenticated party who can set or forge the DNS service record for the seed domain in a connection string can cause the driver to direct its session to an unrelated host and to complete certificate verification against that host instead. This may result in unintended disclosure of application data and of configured database credentials, and in unintended content being returned to the application as query results.

The MongoDB Java Driver does not neutralize NUL characters in the user name and password values it places into the message it builds for SASL PLAIN authentication. A party who can choose the login values that an application passes to the driver can alter where the fields of that message begin and end. This may result in a receiving system reading a login name and secret that differ from the values the application supplied. Authenticating as a different account still requires that account's password. Only deployments that use SASL PLAIN authentication are affected.

A flaw was found in Keycloak. This vulnerability allows an authenticated remote attacker to cause a denial of service by terminating active sessions of arbitrary users. When processing Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) documents that lack a root signature, Keycloak accepts the request as long as any assertion within the document is signed, without verifying its context or placement. An attacker holding a validly signed assertion can embed it into an unsigned logout request for another user, causing Keycloak to accept the forged request and terminate the victim's session.

netty-incubator-codec-ohttp implements Oblivious HTTP (OHTTP) gateway and client functionality using Netty. Prior to 0.0.23.Final, BoringSSLAsymmetricCipherKeyPair.toString in codec-ohttp-hpke-classes-boringssl/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/hpke/boringssl/BoringSSLAsymmetricCipherKeyPair.java includes its private parameter, BoringSSLAsymmetricKeyParameter.toString in codec-ohttp-hpke-classes-boringssl/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/hpke/boringssl/BoringSSLAsymmetricKeyParameter.java renders the complete private-key byte array when isPrivate is true, and BoringSSL.EVP_HPKE_KEY_init_or_throw in codec-ohttp-hpke-classes-boringssl/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/hpke/boringssl/BoringSSL.java includes rejected privateKeyBytes in an exception message. Applications that log affected key-pair objects or initialization exceptions can persist complete HPKE private key material in logs or telemetry. Anyone who can read those records can recover the key and may compromise OHTTP message confidentiality or authenticity expectations while the key remains usable. This issue is fixed in version 0.0.23.Final.

netty-incubator-codec-ohttp implements Oblivious HTTP (OHTTP) gateway and client functionality using Netty. Prior to 0.0.23.Final, BinaryHttpParser in codec-bhttp/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/bhttp/BinaryHttpParser.java accumulates attacker-controlled Binary HTTP variable-length integers into the int offset sumBytes. BinaryHttpParser.readRequestHead, BinaryHttpParser.readFieldLine, and BinaryHttpParser.getIndeterminateLength can narrow long lengths into that offset, causing integer wraparound before buffer indices are calculated. A remote peer that supplies a valid large encoded length to BinaryHttpParser or BinaryHttpDecoder can trigger an unchecked bounds exception from a small malformed message, fail or close the channel, and repeatedly cause denial of service. Java and Netty bounds checks prevent memory corruption, and no information disclosure was observed. This issue is fixed in version 0.0.23.Final.

netty-incubator-codec-ohttp implements Oblivious HTTP (OHTTP) gateway and client functionality using Netty. Prior to 0.0.23.Final, BinaryHttpParser.readFieldLine in codec-bhttp/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/bhttp/BinaryHttpParser.java treats a complete field line that ends exactly at a known field-section boundary as incomplete and returns without consuming bytes. BinaryHttpParser.readFieldSection then leaves fieldSectionLength unchanged and repeats the loop because its forward-progress checks are Java assertions, which are normally disabled in production. A remote peer that sends a known-length Binary HTTP header or trailer section ending at that boundary can make the parser spin indefinitely and pin the Netty event-loop or worker thread responsible for the channel. This issue is fixed in version 0.0.23.Final.

netty-incubator-codec-ohttp implements Oblivious HTTP (OHTTP) gateway and client functionality using Netty. Prior to 0.0.23.Final, BinaryHttpParser.readFieldSection in codec-bhttp/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/bhttp/BinaryHttpParser.java loops while fieldSectionLength is nonzero and relies on disabled-by-default assertions to require BinaryHttpParser.readFieldLine to return a value and consume bytes. A corrupt field line can consume more bytes than its understated declared section length and drive the counter negative, or a truncated field line can return without consuming data and leave the parser in the same state. An unauthenticated OHTTP peer can encrypt such Binary HTTP content under the gateway public configuration, reach OHttpRequestResponseContext.ContentDecoder.decodeChunk, and permanently pin a Netty event-loop thread at full CPU before application business logic. Multiple requests can exhaust the event-loop group and deny service until restart. This issue is fixed in version 0.0.23.Final.

netty-incubator-codec-ohttp implements Oblivious HTTP (OHTTP) gateway and client functionality using Netty. From 0.0.20.Final until 0.0.27.Final, OHttpClientCodec in codec-ohttp/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/ohttp/OHttpClientCodec.java and OHttpServerCodec in codec-ohttp/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/ohttp/OHttpServerCodec.java retain the consumed outer cumulationBuffer after a valid OHTTP exchange completes, even though OHttpRequestResponseContext.destroy in codec-ohttp/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/ohttp/OHttpRequestResponseContext.java releases the inner Binary HTTP cumulation and the channel remains active. A peer can complete a large request or response and leave the keep-alive connection idle, causing the client and server handlers to retain the current high-water pooled or direct buffer capacity until later inbound content replaces it or the handler is removed. Many long-lived idle connections can pin substantial memory and create availability pressure. The issue does not cause unbounded growth for repeated exchanges on a single channel. This issue is fixed in version 0.0.27.Final.
